$$\int_0^x f(t)\,dt = \int_x^1 t^2f(t)\,dt + \frac{x^{16}}{8} + \frac{x^{18}}{9} + c.$$

answer_text:
Let

\[
F(x)=\int_0^x f(t)\,dt
\]

and differentiate both sides of the given equation with respect to \(x\).

The left-hand side differentiates to

\[
\frac{d}{dx}\int_0^x f(t)\,dt=f(x).
\]

For the right-hand side,

\[
\frac{d}{dx}\int_x^1 t^2f(t)\,dt=-x^2f(x),
\]

\[
\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^{16}}{8}+\frac{x^{18}}{9}+c\right)
=2x^{15}+2x^{17}.
\]

Thus,

\[
f(x)=-x^2f(x)+2x^{15}+2x^{17}.
\]

So

\[
(1+x^2)f(x)=2x^{15}(1+x^2).
\]

Since \(1+x^2\neq 0\), we get

\[
f(x)=2x^{15}.
\]

To check consistency with the original equation, substitute \(f(x)=2x^{15}\):

\[
\int_0^x 2t^{15}\,dt=\frac{x^{16}}{8},
\]

and

\[
\int_x^1 t^2(2t^{15})\,dt
=2\int_x^1 t^{17}\,dt
=\frac{1-x^{18}}{9}.
\]

Therefore the right-hand side becomes

\[
\frac{1-x^{18}}{9}+\frac{x^{16}}{8}+\frac{x^{18}}{9}+c
=
\frac{x^{16}}{8}+\frac19+c.
\]

Equating to the left-hand side \(\frac{x^{16}}{8}\) gives

\[
c=-\frac19.
\]

Hence the function is

\[
\boxed{f(x)=2x^{15}}
\]

with the consistency condition \(c=-\frac19\).
